description: Curated, public application help. No learner records, credentials or private admin data.

entries.title: Getting started in DataLearning
entries.answer: Start at the Course Library, choose one of the nine 10-week guided courses, and open Week 1. Each course moves from learning the interface and working with data to analysis, dashboard or report design, and a Week 10 capstone. The separate Career Path explains what to study beyond one tool.
steps: Open Courses and choose a tool or Data Analysis Foundations if you are new.
Read Week 1, download the linked practice file, then complete its learning, practice and knowledge check sections.
Move through the weeks using the course navigation.
When ready, review the Week 10 capstone requirements and submit from your account.

entries.title: Finding and selecting courses
entries.answer: The Course Library includes Data Analysis Foundations, Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, Power Query, Statistics, Python and AI for Data Analysis. Courses have 10 weekly learning stages and practice resources. Choose a course based on your goal rather than completing every course simultaneously.
steps: Open the Course Library.
Use course search and category filters to narrow the list.
Select a course card to open the weekly reader.
Use the week sidebar and Start/Continue options to return to the next lesson.

entries.title: Navigating weeks and lessons
keywords: how do i complete a week
entries.answer: Open a course to see a single-week learning workspace. Use its week navigation to move between Weeks 1–10. Each week has Learn, Practise and Check Knowledge areas plus a completion action. Some courses open directly to a numbered week using the page URL fragment, for example #week8.
steps: Open the relevant course.
Choose your week from the sidebar or Previous/Next controls.
Work through the explanation and exercise, then attempt the knowledge check.
Mark the week complete when you have done the work; your signed-in progress should sync before a capstone.

entries.title: Using Practice Arena
entries.answer: Practice Arena lets you select Excel, SQL or Python practice. Choose a challenge, read the optional Challenge Brief, enter your solution and run the available checks. The Excel worksheet can be shown or hidden. The SQL environment uses SQLite practice queries. The Excel offline formula engine supports a subset of desktop Excel functions; the Python runner also has execution limitations. These environments are not full copies of desktop Excel, every SQL dialect or a local Python installation.
steps: Open Practice Arena and select Excel, SQL or Python.
Choose a challenge and expand Show Brief if you need the requirements.
Write or edit the solution and run the result/check action.
Read the output and feedback; change your solution and rerun.

entries.title: Practice Studio and skill drills
entries.answer: Practice Studio provides short skill-based activities that complement the weekly lessons. It is separate from the editor-based Practice Arena. Pick the course/skill, work on a small task, then return to your weekly lesson.
steps: Open Practice Studio.
Pick a skill or Browse Skills on mobile.
Try the exercise and review feedback.

entries.title: Downloading datasets and weekly worksheets
entries.answer: Each week has matched downloadable practice resources, including a worksheet with tasks and expected deliverables. Excel and Power BI commonly use CSV files; SQL has a ready-to-use SQLite practice database; Python lessons include fictional datasets. Some weeks share a dataset intentionally so you can build on earlier work.
steps: Open the relevant week.
Use the practice dataset or weekly worksheet download in the resource section.
Check the column names and data dictionary before typing formulas or code.
Keep an original copy of the dataset, then work on a duplicate.

entries.title: Watching weekly lesson videos in the app
entries.answer: A lesson video link opens DataLearning’s in-app video dialog. Supported YouTube formats include ordinary watch links, Shorts, some live videos, playlists and timestamps. The video remains hosted by YouTube. Some owners disable embedding or require you to view the video on YouTube; the app cannot override YouTube restrictions.
steps: Open the weekly lesson and choose Watch Lesson Video.
Use the in-app player and fullscreen controls if available.
If embedding is blocked, choose the YouTube fallback to view the video there.
Close the dialog to stop playback and continue the lesson.

entries.title: Submitting a Week 10 capstone project
entries.answer: Week 10 includes a course-specific project brief, required deliverables and a direct submission link. To submit, sign in and complete and sync all 10 weeks for that course. The submission form checks prior review status, accepts up to four supported files, allows up to 12 MB per file and 32 MB total, then routes the project for instructor review. Instructor review, not AI feedback, determines the assessment outcome; the published pass threshold is 70/100.
steps: Open Week 10 of your course and read the full project brief and 100-point rubric.
Prepare your analysis, original project file or notebook, visuals and short evidence-based findings.
Sign in and confirm all ten course weeks are synced as complete.
Select Submit Capstone Project, choose the course and upload your files.
Check your account/submissions page for an instructor decision; AI Tutor cannot approve your work.

entries.title: Learning progress and saved completions
entries.answer: The app provides weekly completion indicators and learner account progress. Some practice or draft states are stored in the browser; signed-in course progress is synced through Supabase when available. A local checkbox is not proof that cloud progress has synced. Sign in to preserve progress across devices and check the course before submitting a capstone.
steps: Open the course and check your week completion indicators.
Sign in to the same learner account across devices.
Allow the progress sync to complete before closing the page.
If it looks wrong, confirm your account and connectivity, then use the account/progress view.

entries.title: Signing in and managing an account
entries.answer: DataLearning uses an account sign-in flow for cloud learner progress, live AI when configured, capstone submissions and some protected learning features. Do not share passwords or verification codes with a tutor. The public course and reference pages can be browsed without giving the tutor personal details.
steps: Open Sign In.
Use your existing account or the available registration/recovery option.
Return to your course and check synced progress.

entries.title: Using the AI Prompt Library
entries.answer: The Prompt Library contains reusable prompts for data cleaning, Excel, SQL, Python, Power BI, analysis and reporting. It is linked directly from the AI for Data Analysis course and its weekly resource area. Treat example prompts as starting points: describe your question and fields accurately, anonymise sensitive data, and verify any AI-generated calculation.
steps: Open the AI course or the Prompt Library directly.
Choose a prompt relevant to your task.
Replace placeholders with synthetic/non-sensitive field names and your own business question.
Use the prompt in an approved AI tool, then independently validate its output.

entries.title: Your Complete Data Career Path
entries.answer: Your Complete Data Career Path is on its own page, separate from the Course Library. It covers four levels—Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced and Expert—with 31 specialist modules spanning analytics, BI, engineering, data science and AI. Those modules contain design exercises and case studies; they do not provision real cloud/Spark/Kafka infrastructure.
steps: Open the Career Path page.
Select a proficiency level or specialist track.
Review the prerequisites and worked case for a module.
Use the nine practical 10-week tool courses to build skills alongside the career roadmap.

entries.title: Using the AI Tutor
entries.answer: Tutor Studio has an offline knowledge guide and optional live AI mode. Offline answers use bundled learning content and the verified app guide; they do not require provider credentials. Live AI uses a server-side OpenAI or Groq key if the administrator has configured one, requires sign-in, and sends your question to the selected provider. Neither mode has access to your private grades, uploaded project files or instructor review decisions.
steps: Open AI Tutor.
Select Offline Guide for bundled explanations, or Live AI if enabled.
Ask a specific question about the app, a course topic, a dataset or an analysis problem.
Use course links supplied in the answer and check computations independently.

entries.title: Quizzes and knowledge checks
entries.answer: Each course week includes a knowledge check or questions page so you can assess understanding. Practice feedback is useful for learning, but it does not replace instructor capstone assessment. Retry after reading the explanation and cross-checking your answer against the lesson.
steps: Open your current course week.
Choose Check Knowledge or Questions to Try.
Answer the questions and review the explanations.
Correct misunderstandings before moving ahead.

entries.title: Certificates and verification
entries.answer: Certificate eligibility follows the published assessment and instructor-review process; simply checking all ten weeks or receiving a Tutor answer is not approval. Existing certificate pages provide verification for an issued certificate.
steps: Complete your course and submit the required capstone.
Wait for an instructor-published assessment outcome.
Use the certificate page for available issuance or verification details.

entries.title: Dashboard design lessons and examples
entries.answer: The 10-week tool journeys include dashboard-layout samples and presentation storyboards in their later weeks. The illustrations show suggested KPI card, chart, filter and insight arrangements. The example images teach visual structure; they are not already-functional dashboard files. You must build and explain your own dashboard or reporting deliverable.
steps: Open the relevant tool course.
Go to Week 8 for dashboard design/layout examples and Week 9 for reporting or presentation.
Recreate a layout using the practice dataset and an appropriate tool.
Write a short insight explaining the chart and the decision it supports.

entries.title: Privacy and safe training data
entries.answer: Use the supplied fictional datasets for lessons and AI prompts. Never paste passwords, tokens, confidential company data or personal customer records into the Tutor or third-party AI providers. Live AI answers are generated from the question and limited chat history, not from a private scan of your account or capstone files.
steps: Use a fictional or anonymised example.
Describe the necessary field names and business rules without revealing identifiers.
Validate all AI results against authorised local sources.

entries.title: Microsoft Excel course — ten-week plan
entries.answer: This course starts with getting comfortable with the excel workspace and builds toward excel analytics capstone: dataset to executive dashboard. It contains ten weeks with instruction, worked examples, datasets and final project guidance.
steps: Week 1: Getting comfortable with the Excel workspace — Identify ribbon tabs, worksheets, cells, ranges and the formula bar before typing or analysing data.
Week 2: Entering, formatting and organising data — Turn raw entries into a well-typed Excel Table that can be filtered without corrupting the source.
Week 3: Essential Excel formulas and cell references — Build correct arithmetic and summary formulas and know when to lock a reference.
Week 4: Cleaning text, dates, duplicates and errors — Fix dirty source data while keeping an auditable record of what changed.
Week 5: IF, SUMIFS, COUNTIFS and lookup functions — Calculate business KPIs by conditions and retrieve attributes from a reference table.
Week 6: PivotTables, dynamic arrays and reusable analysis — Summarise thousands of rows into pivot summaries and dynamic filtered lists without manual recalculation.
Week 7: Choosing and interpreting Excel charts — Create truthful visuals that match the business question and explain what each chart shows.
Week 8: Building a professional interactive Excel dashboard — Arrange KPI cards, PivotCharts and slicers into one readable decision-making page.
Week 9: Writing and presenting an Excel management report — Turn dashboard findings into a concise business narrative and deliver a portable report.
Week 10: Excel analytics capstone: dataset to executive dashboard — Independently design, calculate, validate, present and submit a professional Excel dashboard.

weeks.goal: Build correct arithmetic and summary formulas and know when to lock a reference.

topics.explanation: + - * / act on numeric cells and must use the intended units

topics.explanation: summarise an explicit range rather than typing hardcoded totals

D2 = B2*C2
E2 = D2*$H$2
=SUM(D2:D101) and =AVERAGE(D2:D101)
weeks.task: Compute line revenue, tax using one fixed rate cell, grand total and average order-line value; copy formulas through all rows.
weeks.check: A 3-unit order at 1500 produces 4500 before tax; a fixed 7.5% rate in H2 produces 337.50 tax.
weeks.trap: Hardcoding a tax percentage in every row or confusing gross and net amounts.
weeks.business: A finance assistant needs a dependable daily revenue sheet that recalculates when transactions change.

=IF(OR(D2="",D2<0),"Review","OK")
weeks.task: Create cleaned Region and Status fields, flag blank order dates and suspect amounts, then document how many rows changed.

topics.heading: SUMIFS

topics.heading: COUNTIFS
topics.explanation: count records satisfying multiple tests

=SUMIFS(tblSales[Revenue],tblSales[Region],"North",tblSales[Status],"Paid")

entries.title: Power BI course — ten-week plan
entries.answer: This course starts with touring power bi desktop and its workspace and builds toward power bi capstone: model to published executive report. It contains ten weeks with instruction, worked examples, datasets and final project guidance.
steps: Week 1: Touring Power BI Desktop and its workspace — Recognise the Report, Data and Model views, main ribbon and essential panes without prior Power BI experience.
Week 2: Connecting and profiling data in Power Query — Import spreadsheets or CSVs and identify incorrect types, missing fields and quality problems before modelling.
Week 3: Building relationships and a star schema — Model sales facts with reusable dimension tables to prevent misleading totals and filters.
Week 4: DAX measures and evaluation context — Write measures that react correctly to slicers and compare them with calculated columns.
Week 5: Time intelligence and period comparisons — Analyse month-over-month and year-over-year changes with a proper date dimension.
Week 6: Advanced DAX and analytical scenarios — Control denominators and create context-aware comparisons without confusing totals.
Week 7: Designing Power BI visuals and interactions — Select charts for decisions and make drilldown and filters understandable to a new user.
Week 8: Building a premium interactive Power BI report — Apply grid-based dashboard layout, slicers, bookmarks and visual hierarchy to a decision-ready report page.
Week 9: Publishing, sharing and presenting insights — Explain how Power BI Desktop reports are shared, refreshed and turned into an executive narrative.
Week 10: Power BI capstone: model to published executive report — Build and document an end-to-end data model, DAX KPIs, interactive report and executive presentation.

entries.title: SQL course — ten-week plan
entries.answer: This course starts with understanding databases and sql editor environments and builds toward sql capstone: end-to-end analytical reporting dataset. It contains ten weeks with instruction, worked examples, datasets and final project guidance.
steps: Week 1: Understanding databases and SQL editor environments — Explore a SQL client, tables, schemas and query results before writing your first analytical statement.
Week 2: Writing SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY and LIMIT — Retrieve precise records instead of dumping entire tables to the screen.
Week 3: GROUP BY, aggregation and KPI queries — Turn transaction records into business metrics using grouped aggregations.
Week 4: JOINs, table grain and duplicate control — Combine fact data with reference tables without accidentally multiplying money.
Week 5: CASE, NULL and conditional business rules — Classify transactions transparently and avoid incorrect logic for missing fields.
Week 6: CTEs, subqueries and maintainable reporting SQL — Split a difficult analysis into readable stages that can be checked separately.
Week 7: Window functions and time-based comparisons — Calculate rankings, running totals and period comparisons without losing transaction detail.
Week 8: Building dashboard-ready SQL datasets — Shape a query output that a BI tool can visualise without ambiguity.
Week 9: Optimising, validating and presenting SQL analysis — Explain query results to decision-makers and prepare reproducible validation evidence.
Week 10: SQL capstone: end-to-end analytical reporting dataset — Design, test and submit a repeatable SQL project for a complete business question.

entries.title: Applied Statistics course — ten-week plan
entries.answer: This course starts with discovering statistical tools and data types and builds toward statistics capstone: analysis to executive recommendations. It contains ten weeks with instruction, worked examples, datasets and final project guidance.
steps: Week 1: Discovering statistical tools and data types — Understand how Excel's Analysis ToolPak or Python notebooks support practical statistical questions.
Week 2: Mean, median, mode and interpreting typical values — Calculate central tendency and explain what outliers do to the story.
Week 3: Spread: range, variance and standard deviation — Describe volatility alongside an average rather than hiding unstable results.
Week 4: Frequency tables, histograms and distribution patterns — Create charts that reveal where observations cluster and which values are unusual.
Week 5: Sampling design and identifying bias — Plan a sample that supports a specific conclusion without excluding important customers.
Week 6: Probability and risks in business decisions — Compute basic unconditional and conditional probabilities using observed counts.
Week 7: Correlation and exploratory relationship analysis — Measure associations and explain why they do not automatically establish causation.
Week 8: Confidence intervals and uncertainty dashboard — Construct and interpret a confidence interval in business terms without overstating certainty.
Week 9: Hypothesis testing, experiments and result interpretation — Use clear hypotheses and effect sizes to decide whether an apparent change is meaningful.
Week 10: Statistics capstone: analysis to executive recommendations — Perform descriptive analysis and one defensible inferential check, then present uncertainty to stakeholders.

entries.title: Data Analysis Foundations course — ten-week plan
entries.answer: This course starts with the data analyst's workspace and way of thinking and builds toward data analysis capstone: question to presentation. It contains ten weeks with instruction, worked examples, datasets and final project guidance.
steps: Week 1: The data analyst's workspace and way of thinking — Learn the full analysis workflow and recognise the interfaces analysts commonly use before specialising.
Week 2: Data files, columns, types and measurement — Become confident reading CSVs and spreadsheets and recognising the meaning of each field.
Week 3: Data grain, keys and simple relationships — Understand what one row represents and why duplicates can be legitimate.
Week 4: Understanding and measuring data quality — Identify missing values, erroneous amounts and duplicate keys before trusting a calculation.
Week 5: Basic calculations and descriptive KPIs — Understand totals, counts, averages and the difference between typical and exceptional values.
Week 6: Preparing data for a repeatable analysis — Separate raw source, cleaned records and reporting summaries into traceable layers.
Week 7: Choosing effective charts and reading trends — Connect business questions to line, bar, table and KPI displays without misleading viewers.
Week 8: Planning the first dashboard and selecting KPIs — Design a clean dashboard layout before choosing a complicated tool.
Week 9: Explaining results and writing an executive briefing — Write an evidence-first management report and prepare a brief verbal presentation.
Week 10: Data analysis capstone: question to presentation — Complete one end-to-end analysis using a realistic fictional business dataset.
